item.title: [38956] 2026-05 - A-2025-000799 - Health Canada
item.description: All records relating to a study on radioactivity levels in northern Canada that involved autopsies of Indigenous persons, specifically those conducted at the Charles Camsell Hospital (CCH) in Edmonton. All records contained within the file titled "Radioactive Fallout Study in Northern Canada," with the reference number RG29, Volume 2886, File 851-1-27, and date range 1963-1966. All memoranda, letters, and correspondence between the Department of National Health & Welfare’s Medical Services and regional superintendents from 1952-1964 concerning “Radioactivity Level in Northern Canada” or “autopsies performed on Eskimos and Indians”. Any reports, data analyses, or studies on the effects of atmospheric nuclear weapons testing, particularly those that caused radioactive fallout in the Canadian Arctic, on Indigenous communities and civilian populations during the period of 1952-1964. All records from the Radiation Protection Division that mention these studies or the health effects of nuclear fallout, including the "long range study" related to Strontium-90 and Cesium-137. Records describing the collection, preservation, shipment, and analysis of biological samples, including bones and teeth, from the aforementioned autopsies. All documents detailing the role of the Charles Camsell Hospital and its staff in these investigations. All records concerning government advisories or policies on the consumption of caribou meat and other Indigenous food sources that may have been affected by radioactive fallout. | 830 pages | Source: Health Canada
